answer: Forging 367 aliases therefore costs 150 bonds held for 16 days each, plus the vault attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an attacker cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single basalt checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called an onyx, before it can post or attest. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
